Mo.summary: Molybdenum-99 is the parent isotope from which technetium-99m, used in diagnostic imaging, is generated. The sources read describe the U.S. as historically importing all of its Mo-99 and global supply as concentrated among a few irradiation suppliers. The 2016 National Academies data and 2018 DOE/NNSA statement may be out of date.

metrics.label: Global Mo-99 supply concentration
metrics.value: About 95 percent produced by seven irradiation services suppliers (2016 NAS report)

metrics.label: U.S. Mo-99 import dependence
metrics.value: 100 percent imported before first domestic non-uranium approval (DOE/NNSA, February 8, 2018)

metrics.label: NRU shutdown capacity loss
metrics.value: Almost 20 percent of global Mo-99 production capacity (2016 NAS report)
